messages:
anna (runtime): Quick thread to nail down operator <-> control-plane boundaries for Dedicated GPU pools. Wanted to capture decisions for the autoscaler follow-up.

mike (orch): Good call. Which surfaces are still fuzzy?

anna (runtime): Three sticky ones: authoritative credit ledger, fast local admission (cache/lease pattern), and how we surface overload/backpressure to upper layers and tenants.

priya (infra): Right now infra persists reservations but operators apply decay locally. That split caused a race in last incident where operator evicted but control-plane still counted credits.

mike (orch): We saw double-counting during failover. Operator-local-only decay is the root cause.

dana (eng): Option: move decay into control-plane so there's single source of truth. But that adds latency on admits unless we introduce a fast path.

anna (runtime): Proposal: control-plane = canonical ledger (committed reservations + soft credits). Operator = cached headroom + batched leases for fast admits. Lease = token with qty+expiry issued by control-plane.

mike (orch): Lease model makes sense. Practical: batch minting per tenant/pool to avoid constant control-plane chatter. Operator refills cache by requesting N tokens.

priya (infra): Agree on batching. Also TTLs should be aligned with warmup durations (shorter for small models, longer for big prewarms). If control-plane is unreachable, operator should stop issuing new leases when cache drains and switch to conservative mode.

leo (sre-bot): FYI incident link: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/2025-09-03-prewarm-overlap — same pattern.

sasha (product): From customer POV we need explicit docs for the conservative mode. What happens to traffic?

anna (runtime): UX: affected tenants see degraded cold-start SLOs and optional 503s for low-priority endpoints. We'll expose a flag to map routes to critical vs non-critical and surface signals in Console.

mike (orch): Backpressure signals: operator should emit states: OK, SOFT-THROTTLE (local headroom low), HARD-THROTTLE (no leases). Control-plane and higher-level routers can then react: spin capacity (hosted) or show busy to tenants (Dedicated).

priya (infra): Important: control-plane should not auto-scale Dedicated infra without admin opt-in. For Dedicated, operator should surface the signal and rely on configured policies (customer autoscaler / runbook).

dana (eng): Need billing hooks: who gets charged when burst lanes are used vs steady lanes? Leases should include a billing tag so events are billable.

anna (runtime): Implementation sketch: ledger rows: tenant_id | committed | soft_credits | last_used_ts. Operator cache: map tenant->available, leases:list(lease_id, amount, expires). Admit algo: consume local cache; if miss, request batched lease; if control-plane unavailable, fail-safe to conservative.

mike (orch): Preemption: allow preemptible slices for burst lanes. Define priority classes and a short drain window (e.g., 5s) so RPCs finish. Operator must emit lease_revoked events.

priya (infra): Events: lease_granted, lease_revoked, lease_expired. Stream to cheap topic per region. Also add reconciliation consumer that periodically reconciles ledger vs events to repair drift.

anna (runtime): We'll add an idempotent reconcile endpoint so operator and control-plane can converge after flaky networks. Reconciler reads events and corrects committed counters.

dana (eng): Can we add a chaos harness to validate race conditions? Simulate: control-plane pause, duplicate mint responses, operator restarts mid-lease.

mike (orch): Yes — include tests for batch minting and TTL expiry races. Also smoke test for conservative-mode: ensure operator stops granting after drain.

priya (infra): Rollout plan idea: 1) read-only ledger API deployed so operator can warm up cache from canonical store; 2) opt-in batched lease minting for selected tenants; 3) enable backpressure signals and conservative fallback; 4) enable preemption event hooks behind feature flag.

anna (runtime): Ops checklist matches. I'll update the autoscaler RFC with these boundaries and the lease API sketch today.

sasha (product): I'll draft customer-facing failure-mode text describing increased cold-start times and graceful 503 behaviour.

leo (sre-bot): Reminder: autoscaler follow-up sync tomorrow 10:00 UTC.

mike (orch): I'll own the lease endpoint spec PR and add simple JSON schema for lease events.

anna (runtime): Thanks everyone. If no objections I'll land these notes into the RFC and include a link to the test harness PR.

priya (infra): No objections. :+1:

anna (runtime): Closing thread, will post update here when RFC refreshed.
